description: First a census (names and 30-day message counts only, no message body, never getAllMessages or subscriptions): every team of the tenant, each team's members (TeamMember.Read.All) and each private or shared channel's and chat's members read first and cleared by the shared people guard (integrations/people_exclusion.py) before its name is requested, so a team, channel or chat with an excluded member is refused and counted, never named; then the v1.0 30-day team activity report (Reports.Read.All, one GET). The report answers with a 302 to a CSV download that is never followed: those counts stay null (census.message_counts.status unavailable, reason report_redirect) and the census still completes; only a refused report (403) is a typed block. Names, ids and the proposed purchasing, QA and R&D channels go to a 0600 census file in the state directory (census.file), never to stdout. Message content is read only for the channels and chats the owner's confirmation file names and this census cleared; without one the run is blocked on part teams.content_confirmation, cause later_ask (teams-content-confirmation), never defaulted. Then teams capture through the GET-only Graph client: the channels of the teams cos@ and vince@ joined and the chats of every account on the canonical mail allowlist, operating/case_mail_scope.json, derived from it on every run (examples/teams_capture_scope.live-check.json, member_chats mail_allowlist; docs/decisions/2026-10-07-ovs-teams-capture.md item 2), each channel's and chat's membership read first as the audience of its messages (this command no longer falls back to a team's Microsoft 365 group: a team whose members read answers 403 is a blocked part naming TeamMember.Read.All), channel message delta with replies and chat messages (newest first, then lastModifiedDateTime since the high-water), into the host's Workbench state directory for this check ($PLX_WORKBENCH_STATE_DIR/teams-capture-check/live when that variable is set, an absolute path, else $XDG_STATE_HOME/plx-workbench/teams-capture-check/live, else under $HOME/.local/state; storage.state_base names which base; outside the git tree, kept across the check's daily runs, the eval.heldout pattern). A later run (run 2, or the next day's first run) resumes from the stored cursor or delta link; an invocation stops at the first run that completes a pass and never starts a new one after it. Beyond max_conversations the runs rotate on the same state until one full pass is read (every conversation found read complete; one cut short is read again when the rotation comes round), at most 12 runs and 6300 s (--budget-seconds: no run starts and no read goes on to its next page after it; pass.stop names what ended the runs, budget.exhausted whether the budget did); a pass not finished carries over to the next daily run. pass.last_run_complete and pass.unvisited_falling (counted over the conversations the first run found, pass.unvisited_first_run: never rises and ends below its start or at 0; a conversation created mid-pass is read in the pass but never flips it) are asserted. Then the store is read back offline as a member (what it sees resolves), as an outsider granted every conversation but a member of none (sees 0) and as a withheld principal (sees 0). Graph application permissions needed: ChannelMessage.Read.All and Chat.Read.All (Microsoft protected APIs: app-only access needs Microsoft's approval besides admin consent), Channel.ReadBasic.All, TeamMember.Read.All, ChannelMember.Read.All, ChatMember.Read.All, Team.ReadBasic.All, Chat.ReadBasic.All, User.Read.All and Reports.Read.All (the census counts; later_ask graph-teams-consent). A 403 from Graph is reported as blocked_upstream with error_code missing_permission and the Graph permission the refused read needs, never as a pass; a run blocked by Graph consent (403), by the absent owner confirmation, or by both, is a typed block (expect_blocked), with the census counts recorded whenever consent let it run; a chat read refused names its own part (teams.chats, teams.chat_members or teams.chat_messages) beside any channel part (teams.members, teams.messages), never in its place. summary.chats counts the chats captured. Counts, booleans and enums only.
notes: Live-unverified: written and checked against the injected-transport fixture run only (integrations/tests/test_capture_teams.py, ProbeTests runs this argv over a fake Graph whose directory holds every allowlisted account; evidence label injected-transport). Live so far: both runs reported discovery incomplete on cap:conversation_cap (max_conversations 6, the same first 6 every run, 204 of 900 s) and the members group fallback served 6 of 6. Discovery now records discovered_total, rotates past the cap on a cursor kept in the capture store and reports unvisited; a conversation counts as visited only when its latest read finished complete. The check carries its state across its own runs until one full pass completes (owner decision 2026-10-10-followup-decisions.md item 17): the store lives in the host state directory, not {tmp}, so the rotation (layout version 2; an older layout restarts the pass, never reports it complete) and every resumable read carry on into the next daily run (storage.carried). Within an invocation: --runs 2, then on, at most --max-runs 12 and --budget-seconds 6300, and it stops at the first run that completes a pass (never a new pass after it, so pass and unvisited_falling are about the current pass only; the day a carried pass completes passes with pass.stop complete) (16 conversations a run, about 544 s each; the budget leaves 600 s of the 6900 s timeout, under the 7200 s runtime command limit, for the read-back; caps not raised). A pass not finished within one day's budget reports status incomplete with pass.stop budget or max_runs and fails status and pass.last_run_complete that day, never passes; it is expected complete within a few daily runs. Cross-container persistence (a fresh container starts the pass over) waits on the durable capture store (later_ask durable-capture-store). runs[*].discovery.status is no longer asserted per run: run 1 is capped whenever more than 16 conversations exist. A refused permission still reports blocked (expect_blocked, cause host_misconfiguration), never a pass. Expected when permitted: run 1 round full, a conversation's next read (the next run, or the next day's when the pass completed) round incremental with resumed_from delta_url (or cursor while a cap stopped run 1); a channel cut by max_pages_per_run 3 stays incomplete with reason cap:page_cap, keeps the pass open and resumes on its next turn. Unverified live assumptions: Graph answers app-only /users/{id}/joinedTeams and /users/{id}/chats, also for an allowlisted shared mailbox without Teams (else that account's read is a source error or a blocked teams.chats part, named in runs[*].discovery.reasons); a standard channel's audience equals its team's members; channel delta nextLink/deltaLink keep the request's path (the guard refuses any other); run 2 of a chat relies on chat messages accepting $filter lastModifiedDateTime gt with $orderby lastModifiedDateTime desc; a reply added to an unchanged root is listed by the delta (else captured at the next full round). Members fallback: no longer used by this command (the census clears each team's own members through the people guard before its name; integrations/tests/test_capture_teams_members_fallback.py). Census and owner confirmation: injected transport only (integrations/tests/test_capture_teams_census.py); live-unverified: the report row shape (teamId, details[].channelMessages) and that the v1.0 report answers 302 (counts null, census complete). registry_names: the source registry credits a Graph endpoint template only through operations_read, the grammar operations (integrations/live_source_grammar.py) this run's GETs were answered for; an endpoint no operation folds to is never credited by this check.
